title: Look up a part's construction capabilities before attaching it
applicability: Use when an official LDraw part can be found but an expected connector cannot. Inspect the active BrickLayer catalog version and the relevant capability records before choosing a workaround.
aliases: part exists but has no connectors
steps: Call lookup_part with the exact part ID and inspect its constructible, collision and connectivity records separately. Inspect endpoints on the part you want to attach and on its mate. A part number or a usable bounding box does not determine which connections the current release can validate.

For 2651, inspect the current capabilities and compare its documented endpoints with the intended mate on 2650. Decide based on the returned version and evidence. The missing-annotations example uses 10040, a constructible part that has a collision body but no annotated connector.

If a relevant annotation is missing, report the part number, release and missing capability. When changing the design is acceptable, choose a pair with well-described ports. The example demonstrates the fallback workflow with a paired finger hinge for a revised hinge design.
expected: The catalog example reads the live 2651 capability and verifies missing_connector_annotations for the 10040 fixture. The alternative finger hinge connects, clears the meshes and passes its declared motion samples.

sources.author: Carlos Antelo
sources.title: Connector evidence and snapping
sources.adaptation: Reference only. Nova's ability to distinguish model geometry from connector annotations motivated this diagnosis. The example reads BrickLayer's own catalog. The BrickWright guidance and example are original.
